div.div:
Default an API key
One field: API Key. Works on a hosted or a self-hosted gateway.
Managed self-hosted on Azure only
One optional field: Azure Managed ClientID, needed only for a
user-assigned identity. Nothing is stored, so nothing rotates.
Azure Entra a service principal
Azure Entra ClientID, Azure Entra Secret, Azure Entra Tenant ID,
plus a Use Entra Federated Authentication checkbox.
Workload Identity self-hosted on Azure only
Azure Workload ClientID and Azure Workload Tenant ID. This is
Azure AD workload identity. There is no token endpoint and no
service account ID, so it is not the Open AI style of federation.

div.div:
One integration carries many deployments. Each entry has:
• Deployment Name — what the caller sends in the model field
• Alias Name — purpose not confirmed in a tenant
• API Version — per entry, defaults to v1, editable
• Foundation Model — a dropdown of Azure models
• Make it default model — checked by default
Add entries with + Add Model or + From Target URI.
Use the same api-version your applications already send. Changing
it changes the request contract, not just a label.
Azure Foundry is a different tile and works differently: one Azure
Target URI and one optional deployment name, with no model picker.

div.div:
In Azure you give a name to a model when you deploy it, and that name is
what every caller must use. A call naming gpt-4o fails when the
deployment is called prod-chat, even though the model behind it is
exactly that.
Collect deployment names before the work session. Do not collect model
names, because they are not what the application sends.
Three products share the Azure name and none is interchangeable:
Azure OpenAI is this tile. Azure Foundry is a separate tile. Microsoft
Copilot Studio is a different product on a different runtime.

div.div:
1. Azure bills your subscription for inference. Unchanged by the
gateway. Same resource, same rates, same cost analysis blade.
2. Palo Alto Networks meters flex credits by token volume.
1 token = 4 characters. Prompts, MCP, and agent-to-agent traffic all
count. Identical pricing for SaaS and Hybrid.
Azure OpenAI is Open AI compatible, so the streaming trap applies here
too. Without stream_options: {include_usage: true} the provider
returns no usage data, tokens and cost log as zero, and the budget
never sees the spend.
